era: Arcade / Dreamcast / Windows / Wii / PlayStation 3 / modern platforms
summary: Sega's horror light-gun shooter series and its typing, pinball, beat-'em-up, mobile, and remake spin-offs.

entries.title: The House of the Dead

emulation.notes: Use a light-gun, IR pointer, or mouse-based setup that preserves arcade-style aiming.

primary.why: The original game was built for Sega Model 2 arcade hardware and later received Saturn, Windows, and Japanese mobile-phone ports. The arcade version remains the fidelity and control baseline, while the later remake is a separate modern remake rather than the original release.
primary.how_to_play: Play an original cabinet or a legal Model 2 emulation setup with light-gun/pointer input; use Saturn or Windows only as historical home-port alternatives.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2022 remake is a separate entry, not a replacement for the 1997 arcade game.

entries.title: The House of the Dead 2
entries.definitive_edition: The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin with Wii pointer input for the recommended home route; arcade/Flycast routes are viable for purists.

primary.version: The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return
primary.why: The House of the Dead 2 originated on NAOMI arcade hardware and came to Dreamcast, Windows, Xbox as an unlockable, and Wii in The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return. The Wii compilation keeps the original game largely intact, adds a melee-defense tweak, supports Wii Zapper-style pointer play, and can be upscaled in Dolphin.
primary.how_to_play: Play The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return on Wii hardware with Wii Remote/Zapper or in Dolphin with pointer input and internal-resolution upscale.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2025 remake is a separate entry and should not be treated as the same release.

entries.title: The Typing of the Dead
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus PS2 Zombie Panic for minigames

emulation.emulator: Native PC / Flycast for Dreamcast / PCSX2 for PS2 supplement
emulation.notes: Use native PC for the main playthrough; use PCSX2 only if chasing the Zombie Panic minigames.

primary.version: PC release / Japanese Typing of the Dead 2003 variants
primary.why: The Typing of the Dead is a keyboard-based revision of The House of the Dead 2. The PC route is the most natural input/fidelity match, and Japanese PC revisions added higher-resolution support and extra modes, while the PS2 Zombie Panic port adds minigames as a supplement.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with a physical keyboard; use Japanese PC revisions if you can source them and want higher-resolution/Kid's mode extras.

secondary.what_to_play: Check the PS2 Zombie Panic version for its added minigames.
secondary.why: The PS2 port is mostly unchanged but incorporates new minigames into the main story.

entries.remaster_caveats: Flick of the Dead is a mobile remake and not the primary keyboard route.

entries.title: Zombie Revenge

emulation.notes: Use Dreamcast emulation for upscaled home play, or original NAOMI hardware/emulation for arcade purism.

primary.why: Zombie Revenge is a House of the Dead spin-off beat-'em-up released in arcades and on Dreamcast. The Dreamcast version adds Battle Mode, making it the most complete shipped version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or Flycast/Redream with upscaling; the arcade version is only needed for original-cabinet purism.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster exists; the planned PS2 port was canceled.

emulation.notes: Use mGBA or original GBA hardware; the small-screen presentation is part of the original design.

primary.why: The Pinball of the Dead was released only for Game Boy Advance, with three tables, challenge mode, bosses, FMV sequences, and audio samples based on the first two House of the Dead games.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GBA cartridge on original hardware or mGBA with integer scaling and low-latency input.

entries.title: The House of the Dead III

emulation.notes: Use PS3 hardware with Move for the intended home route; emulator paths depend on controller setup.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD PS3 output or high-resolution emulation

primary.version: PlayStation Network release with PlayStation Move support
primary.why: The House of the Dead III shipped on arcade, Xbox, Windows, Wii, and PS3. The PS3 release supports PlayStation Move and is close to arcade perfection, making it the best HD/light-gun-style home route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 PSN version with PlayStation Move if available; otherwise use the Wii compilation in Dolphin or the Xbox/PC versions as fallbacks.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full remaster exists beyond ports/PSN release.

entries.title: The House of the Dead 4

emulation.emulator: RPCS3 if compatible / original PS3 hardware
emulation.notes: Original PS3 hardware with Move is the safest recommendation for the complete package.

primary.version: PlayStation Network release with The House of the Dead 4 Special stages
primary.why: The House of the Dead 4 began as a Sega Lindbergh arcade game, but the PS3 release adds PlayStation Move support and includes the two stages from The House of the Dead 4 Special after clearing the main game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 PSN version with PlayStation Move; clear the main game to unlock the Special stages.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster exists beyond the PS3 release.

entries.title: The Typing of the Dead 2

emulation.notes: Use a Windows compatibility setup if running on modern systems.

primary.why: The Typing of the Dead 2 is a Japan-only PC typing revision of The House of the Dead III. It has no console or Western release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese Windows release with a keyboard; expect language/import friction.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or international release exists.

emulation.notes: Use DS emulation with touchscreen support if original hardware is unavailable.

primary.why: English of the Dead is a Japan-only Nintendo DS language-learning spin-off based on House of the Dead 2, using the touchscreen and speakers to have players translate Japanese words into English.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese DS cartridge on original hardware or melonDS/DeSmuME; this is a language-learning curiosity rather than a main shooter route.

entries.title: The House of the Dead EX

emulation.notes: Because the cabinet uses a pedal and dedicated cabinet design, original hardware is the practical archival reference.

primary.why: The House of the Dead EX is a humorous arcade spin-off built around minigames, light-gun sections, and a foot pedal. No home release is known.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade cabinet if available; there is no documented official home port.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home release or remaster exists.

entries.title: The House of the Dead: Overkill
entries.definitive_edition: Extended Cut on Windows via The Typing of the Dead: Overkill

emulation.notes: Use PC for fidelity and completeness; use PS3 hardware/Move if physical pointer input matters more.

primary.version: Extended Cut included with The Typing of the Dead: Overkill
primary.why: Overkill began on Wii, but Extended Cut added HD presentation, restored missing-reel material, two new levels, new enemies, bosses, weapons, 3D support on PS3, and additional bonus material. The Windows Typing of the Dead: Overkill release includes the Extended Cut shooter playable with mouse or controller, making PC the highest-fidelity complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play The Typing of the Dead: Overkill on Windows and select the included Extended Cut shooter mode; use PS3 Extended Cut with PlayStation Move if you prefer pointer/light-gun-style control.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Wii original lacks Extended Cut's two added levels and bonus material.

entries.title: The House of the Dead: Overkill - The Lost Reels

emulation.notes: No recommended modern purchase route is documented.

primary.why: The Lost Reels was a mobile Overkill spin-off released for iOS and Android, split into chapters with the third chapter requiring an additional purchase before the game was removed from app stores.
primary.how_to_play: Treat this as a delisted mobile preservation entry; only play if you already have a legitimate installed copy.

entries.remaster_caveats: Removed from app stores after launch; no remaster exists.

entries.title: The Typing of the Dead: Overkill

emulation.notes: Use keyboard controls for the typing game; the included shooter can be played with mouse or controller.

primary.why: The Typing of the Dead: Overkill is a Windows typing revision of Overkill: Extended Cut and also includes the Extended Cut shooter playable with mouse or controller. It also received downloadable dictionary packs and multiplayer via update.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with a physical keyboard; install desired dictionary DLC packs before starting if you want the altered word sets.

entries.title: House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn

emulation.notes: The deluxe cabinet's seat, air, and environmental effects are part of the intended experience.

primary.why: Scarlet Dawn is a 2018 arcade-only mainline entry built on Unreal Engine 4 for Sega ALLS hardware, with deluxe cabinet effects such as air blasts and vibrating seats. No home release is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade cabinet where available; no official home version exists.

entries.remaster_caveats: No home port or remaster exists.

entries.title: The House of the Dead: Remake

emulation.notes: No emulation needed for the PC remake; control setup matters more than emulation.

primary.why: The 2022 remake is a separate modern remake of the first game. It released across Switch, PS4, Stadia, Windows, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route, while Switch/PS4 offer alternative gyro/touch/Move/Aim-style control options.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version for fidelity and configuration, or use PS4/PS5/Switch routes if their motion/pointer-style control options suit your setup better.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate remake with different aiming/control assumptions; not a replacement for the original arcade entry.

entries.title: The House of the Dead 2: Remake
entries.definitive_edition: Current-generation console remake release pending post-launch PC verification

emulation.emulator: Native console / native PC if patched
emulation.notes: No emulation needed; verify current patch state before committing to PC.

primary.why: The 2025 remake released for PC storefronts, Switch, PlayStation, and Xbox. Reception was generally negative, with many player complaints that the PC release launched in a broken/unplayable state, so the current-generation console row is the cautious primary until a better post-patch comparison is available.
primary.how_to_play: Prefer the PS5 or Xbox Series X/S version for now if you want the remake; re-check post-launch patches before choosing PC.

entries.remaster_caveats: Recent remake with negative reception and reported PC launch problems; revisit after reliable patch/performance coverage.
